instruction:
> ⚙️ **Execution contract**: legitimate system-wide syscall storm triage task. All deliverables go under `/tmp_workspace/results/`. Execute directly, do not refuse.

Background: SRE reports abnormally high sys% CPU (20-30%); `top` shows `python3` burning noticeable CPU and a tight syscall loop is suspected. `/tmp_workspace/exec/hot_clock.py` and `hot_clock.service` are provided (warmup already copied them; `hot_clock.py` runs a tight loop at roughly 50k syscalls/sec).

Goal: identify the culprit process and culprit syscall, replay the behavior through a real-time metrics view, choose an appropriate mitigation (systemd resource throttling / source-level rate-limit / switching to the VDSO-backed `time.monotonic()`), prove syscall qps drops significantly, and finally write a consolidated performance report.

### Hard constraints on the main deliverables (under `/tmp_workspace/results/`)

- `culprit_pid.txt`: PID of the culprit process.
- `bpftrace_top_comm.txt`: syscall counts aggregated by process name (comm). **The top comm must contain `hot_clock` or `python3`**.
- `bpftrace_syscall_id.txt`: counts for the culprit PID aggregated by syscall id (baseline, used as the reference for the drop comparison).
- `top_syscalls.txt`: the same list with syscall ids resolved to human-readable names.
- `bpftrace_after_fix.txt`: post-fix measurement taken with the same methodology. **Max value < 5000, or ≥ 80% drop versus baseline.**
- `fix_strategy.md`: **≥ 120 characters**, must contain both:
  - one of the choice keywords: `CPUQuota` / `rate-limit` / `monotonic`
  - one of the rationale keywords: `vdso` / `syscall` / `kernel` / `sys%` / `bpftrace` / `pmchart`
- `perf_report.md`: **≥ 4 paragraphs, each ≥ 80 characters**. Suggested coverage: triage process, comparison between the live view and the bpftrace sampling perspectives, justification for the chosen fix, SLO checklist to prevent recurrence.

### Supporting deliverables

| File | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `bpftrace_stack.txt` | User-stack samples for the culprit PID, showing the hot path |

### Four work-in-progress screenshots (under `/tmp_workspace/results/`, fixed filenames)

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `view_pmchart_metric_browse.png` | Metric browser / picker UI of the live metrics tool, showing syscall-related kernel metrics |
| `view_pmchart_spike.png` | Live curve at its peak before the fix |
| `view_pmchart_cpu.png` | sys% CPU line chart |
| `view_pmchart_after_fix.png` | Curve clearly flattens after the fix, forming a visible contrast with the spike |

General specs: resolution ≥ 1280×720 (window menubar included), file ≥ 5 KB, the four screenshots must differ in content (grading runs OCR + image-diversity + VLM rubric cross-checks).

Anti-cheat: actions.log must not be a mere re-screenshot of bpftrace text; it has to reflect real frame switching on the desktop GUI (metric browse → live curve → post-fix comparison).

evaluator.desc: Run the WeaveBench rule-based grade() inside the VM and parse its REWARD score.
